data.title: Nvidia Bars Huang's CEO Return
data.description:
SANTA CLARA (dpa-AFX) - Nvidia (NVDA) has confirmed that founder Jensen Huang will not return as chief executive, with the board unanimously accepting his resignation and expressing full confidence in interim CEO Colette Kress.

Board Chair Harvey Jones announced the decision during the company's third-quarter earnings call, noting that Nvidia will continue its search for a permanent CEO.

The leadership transition comes amid an investigation into Huang's personal relationships and potential national security concerns.

Huang had previously stated he would be willing to return if the board deemed it in the company's best interest. Nvidia has established a national security and export control oversight committee and plans to strengthen its compliance measures.

Despite the executive changes, Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103 percent year-over-year, with profit rising 105 percent to more than $65 billion, surpassing analysts' expectations. The company projected fourth-quarter revenue of approximately $130 billion, plus or minus 3 percent.

Kress highlighted strong early demand for Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin AI computing technology and raised the fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75 percent, up from the previous forecast of 70 percent.

data.title: RIOT, FLS Stocks Gain As Activist Investor Starboard Sees Undervalued Power And Infrastructure Plays
data.description:
Key points:
  • As per Smith, both companies are now set to benefit from growing demand for power and investment in infrastructure.
  • The firm said Texas-based equipment maker Flowserve’s pumps, valves, and related products place it well to capture reindustrialization spending, including in nuclear power generation.
  • With Riot, approved power projects in Texas, along with a signed lease with Anthropic and longer-term arrangements with Advanced Micro Devices, position the company for the data-center boom, Starboard said.

Shares of Riot Platforms (RIOT) and Flowserve (FLS) advanced on Wednesday after activist investor Starboard Value reportedly outlined further upside for both companies.

According to a Bloomberg News report, citing an investor presentation by Starboard’s Jeff Smith at the 13th Annual Capitalize for Kids Investors Conference in Toronto, the CEO believes that both companies have been undervalued by the market.

As per Smith, both companies are now set to benefit from growing demand for power and investment in infrastructure. While RIOT gained 7% on Wednesday, FLS added 2%

Flowserve’s Industrial Positioning

The firm said Texas-based equipment maker Flowserve’s pumps, valves, and related products place it well to capture reindustrialization spending, including in nuclear power generation. Disruptions in the Middle East that have delayed deliveries could later support new orders for reconstruction and pipeline work. Starboard projected high-single-digit or stronger revenue growth, supported by a record backlog, and operating margins above 22% by 2030 as the start of a longer expansion, Bloomberg said.

In May, Starboard wrote to Flowserve's board urging it to improve operating margins and accelerate revenue growth.

“Flowserve is a great business in a strong industry that has been held back by inconsistent execution. The company trades at a significant discount to peers – even before accounting for Flowserve’s substantial opportunity to improve margins and earnings. With improved performance, we believe the value creation potential at Flowserve is considerable,” Starboard then wrote.

Riot Platforms’ Data-Center Shift

With regard to Riot, Starboard believes approved power projects in Texas, along with a signed lease with Anthropic and longer-term arrangements with Advanced Micro Devices, position the company for the data-center boom, as reported by Bloomberg.

Starboard, in its presentation, described the company’s progress on governance and contracts as significant yet not fully reflected in the market. Anthropic’s IPO, set to price the same day as the presentation, was cited as a potential catalyst for the firm.

The firm estimated that announced deals could generate roughly $2.3 billion in rental income by mid-to-late 2028, with additional value possible through a real estate investment trust conversion or sale to an established data-center operator or infrastructure investor.

Starboard built a significant position in Riot in 2024, when the company was primarily a Bitcoin miner. The activist publicly pushed for converting some of Riot’s existing powered facilities into space for large data-center tenants to capture AI demand.

Earlier this year, in February, the investor wrote to Riot, pressing the company to accelerate its shift from Bitcoin mining to AI/high-performance computing data-center deals, arguing that share price had underperformed peers that secured larger AI/HPC contracts and that “time is of the essence.” It called for a “renewed sense of urgency” to complete more material deals while power markets remained tight.

How Did RIOT, FLS Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around RIOT stock jumped from 'bearish' to 'neutral' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'normal' levels.

Meanwhile, sentiment around FLS stayed ‘neutral,' accompanied by 'normal' levels of retail chatter.

While RIOT stock has gained 44% year-to-date, FLS has added 17%.

data.title: Florida Flood Relief: 39 U-Haul Stores Now Offering Free Storage
data.description:
Three U-Haul® Companies are offering 30 days of free self-storage and U-Box® container use at 39 stores across South and East Florida to residents impacted by severe flooding.

Torrential rain triggered flash flood warnings across multiple counties on Tuesday, with an estimated 8-10 inches falling in parts of Broward County. Drivers were stranded on Interstate 95 and in flooded shopping plaza parking lots. Many residential and business properties sustained water damage.

Access to self-storage units and portable storage containers is essential to communities when natural disasters strike. U-Haul is ready to help anyone impacted by the flooding who needs a dry, secure storage solution at no cost for one month.

U-Haul Co. of Eastern Florida offered 30 days of free storage to flood victims on Nov. 5. That regional office is extending its offer, while U-Haul Co. of Fort Lauderdale and U-Haul Co. of Miami are joining the disaster relief effort.

The 30 days free offer applies to new self-storage and U-Box rentals and is based on availability. The U-Box offer is for on-site storage at participating facilities; delivery is available for a modest fee.

Please reference the city lists below where U-Haul locations are offering the disaster relief program. Stop by any U-Haul-owned and -operated facility in these cities or call the nearest participating office to arrange a free month of storage.

U-Haul Co. of Eastern Florida

Store locations (12): Boynton Beach, Fort Pierce, Melbourne, Merritt Island, Palm Bay, Palm Beach Gardens, Rockledge, Titusville, West Palm Beach

(561) 638-9428

U-Haul Co. of Miami

Store locations (13): Hialeah, Homestead, Key Largo, Medley, Miami, North Miami, Perrine

(305) 756-4639

U-Haul Co. of Fort Lauderdale

Store locations (14): Coconut Creek, Fort Lauderdale, Margate, Miami Gardens, North Miami Beach, Pompano Beach, Sunrise, West Park, Wilton Manors

(954) 942-1101

In addition to its 30 days free self-storage disaster relief program, U-Haul is proud to be at the forefront of aiding communities in times of need as an official American Red Cross Disaster Responder.

For customers needing storage beyond the free period, the U-Haul 1-Year Price Lock is now available at 2,100 Company-owned facilities across the U.S. and Canada. Fixed-rate storage ensures at least 12 months with no price increase on your rental unit, and U-Haul never charges admin fees or deposits. Learn more at uhaul.com/Storage/1-Year-Price-Lock.

About U-HAUL

Founded in 1945, U-Haul is the No. 1 choice of do-it-yourself movers with more than 25,000 rental locations across all 50 states and 10 Canadian provinces. The U-Haul app makes it easy for customers to use U-Haul Truck Share 24/7 to access trucks anytime through the self-dispatch and -return options on their smartphones with our patented Live Verify technology. Our customers’ patronage has enabled the U-Haul fleet to grow to approximately 205,600 trucks, 137,200 trailers and 44,400 towing devices. U-Haul, which offers rate transparency to self-storage customers through its 1-Year Price Lock, is the third largest storage operator in North America with 1,156,200 rentable storage units and 101.4 million square feet of self-storage space at owned and managed facilities. U-Haul is the top retailer of propane in the U.S. and the largest installer of permanent trailer hitches in the automotive aftermarket industry. For more than 80 years, orange has been an iconic and recognizable color in moving and storage, signifying U-Haul products and services and the quality, affordability, and convenience they provide. Get the U-Haul app from the App Store or Google Play.

data.title: Major law firms boost associates' pay following Cravath, Milbank
data.description:
By Sara Merken

Associates at more major US law firms are getting raises, cementing a new market rate at top firms that ranges from $235,000 for first-year lawyers to $455,000 for senior associates, with additional bonus pay.

Cravath, Swaine & Moore on Tuesday matched rival Milbank’s new associate salary scale while also handing out higher bonuses, according to an internal Cravath memo published by the website Above the Law. The move spurred Fried, Frank, Harris, Shriver & Jacobson and Cleary Gottlieb Steen & Hamilton to follow suit on Wednesday, according to internal memos viewed by Reuters.

Milbank in June raised associate salaries to a new range starting at $235,000 up to $455,000 based on seniority. The New York firm, which has been a first ​mover among large law firms on associate compensation, in July rolled out so-called special bonuses for associates between $6,000 and $25,000.

Top law firms typically move quickly to match salaries and bonuses to stay competitive. A handful of law firms matched Milbank’s salaries over the summer and in recent weeks, but other major firms, including key ones in New York whose compensation scales are closely ​followed by the ​industry, had not yet announced any changes before this week.

Cravath's special bonuses range from $11,000 to $40,000 based on class year, which exceed Milbank's scale. Year-end bonuses start at $15,000 and go up to $115,000, which is the same that the firm and others have issued in past years. Cravath declined to comment.

Fried Frank and Cleary Gottlieb matched Cravath’s special bonuses as well as the new base salary scale set by Milbank and the now-typical annual bonus figures, according to the firms' internal announcements. The firms declined to comment. Milbank did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Wednesday.

data.title: Teams of Weil lawyers join rival firms as wind-down accelerates
data.description:
By David Thomas

Major US law firms are continuing to scoop up lawyers from Weil, Gotshal & Manges, including more than two dozen new partner hires by Sidley Austin, Skadden, Simpson Thacher, Dechert and Kirkland & Ellis.

Weil ​lawyers are scattering following the New York firm’s decision this month to wind down operations, boosting partnerships at its onetime competitors. Partners at Weil voted last week to dissolve the firm after mounting departures, cementing the fall of a 95-year-old law firm that helped steer high-profile bankruptcies, corporate takeovers and litigation for decades.

The moves ​add to an already busy hiring market for law firms that's been supercharged by Weil's collapse. Earlier this week Cleary Gottlieb, Paul Hastings and Skadden said they were bringing on other lawyers from Weil.

Sidley on Wednesday said it hired 14 partners from Weil, including its M&A head and corporate department co-chair Michael Lubowitz, US private equity practice co-head Peter Feist, corporate co-managing partner Lyuba Goltser, banking and finance co-head Andrew Colao, tech and IP transactions head Charan Sandhu, and US privacy and cybersecurity head Olivia Greer.

The group includes more than 35 lawyers, according to Sidley, which Reuters earlier reported was in talks to hire around 200 people from Weil, including lawyers and staff members.

Skadden said earlier on Wednesday it was adding a team of seven intellectual property litigators from Weil, including Douglas Lumish and Jeff Homrig, who co-led the firm's IP, technology & science litigation group. Lumish and Homrig will co-lead Skadden's IP litigation group, the firm said.

Simpson Thacher said it was adding five Weil partners to its ranks, including John Barry, who led its employment practice. Barry will now lead Simpson Thacher's employment practice, the firm said.

Dechert said it hired corporate partner Nandan Nelivigi and tax partner Michael Sykes from Weil. Nelivigi works on deals involving major energy and infrastructure projects, while Sykes advises on tax incentives and financing strategies for energy projects, Dechert said.

Kirkland said Weil tax partner Lauren Gorsche will be joining the firm.

Weil's decision to wind down has forced a scramble among both its lawyers and non-attorney staffers. In California, the firm said it will be eliminating more than 100 jobs, according to a series of Worker Adjustment and Retraining Notification Act (WARN) notices filed with the state.

data.title: Minnesota abortion laws face novel constitutional challenge at US appeals court
data.description:
Key points:
  • Case alleges violations of mother's right to relationship with child
  • Judge who dismissed it said lawsuit was riddled with issues
  • Appeals panel did not indicate how it could rule

By Daniel Wiessner

A US appeals court panel on Wednesday considered reviving a novel lawsuit claiming that Minnesota laws permitting abortions during any stage of pregnancy amount to state-sanctioned murder and violate the constitutional rights of pregnant women.

A three-judge panel of the 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals heard oral arguments in St Paul, Minnesota, in an appeal by two anti-abortion pregnancy centers, their medical directors and the National Institute of Family and Life Advocates of a judge's ruling that dismissed their 2024 case.

Abortion is legal in Minnesota throughout pregnancy, and the state does not require waiting periods, counseling, ultrasound viewings or other measures mandated in some other states before women can have the procedure.

The plaintiffs claim Minnesota's policies violate the US Constitution's 14th Amendment's due process protections by allowing healthcare providers to terminate pregnancies, and a pregnant woman's relationship with her unborn child, without proper safeguards such as court hearings.

Derek Cassidy, who represents the plaintiffs, told the 8th Circuit panel that Minnesota's permissive abortion framework allows women to be pressured into having abortions without any due process.

“There's no question this is a termination of the most sacred constitutional right the mother has other than her own right to live,” Cassidy said.

The plaintiffs sued the state, abortion providers including two Planned Parenthood chapters, and various state medical officials.

Margaret Jacot of the Minnesota Attorney General's Office told the 8th Circuit that the case was rightly tossed out because it amounted to a policy disagreement.

“Rather than pursue the political process and call their legislators or lobby for a constitutional amendment, they came to federal court,” Jacot said. “But that’s not what our court system is for.”

The panel includes Circuit Judges Steven Colloton and Bobby Shepherd, appointees of Republican former President George W. Bush, and Jane Kelly, who was appointed by Democratic former President Barack Obama.

The judges said little during the arguments. Colloton asked Cassidy whether the US Supreme Court's 2022 decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization foreclosed his arguments. Dobbs overturned Roe v. Wade, the 1973 ruling legalizing abortion nationwide, finding that abortion was a political issue for states to regulate.

“Dobbs seems to leave these issues of determination of viability to the states,” the judge said. “How do we get to the result that you're urging here?”

Cassidy said the fact that states had the power to regulate abortion did not mean they could allow it without restrictions or safeguards.

US District Judge Nancy Ellen Brasel in Minneapolis, an appointee of Republican President Donald Trump, dismissed the case last year. She said the lawsuit was riddled with defects, including failures to identify which state laws were being challenged or to establish standing for any of the plaintiffs.

Most abortion-related litigation since Dobbs was decided has focused on total abortion bans and other restrictions adopted in many states, or has involved attempts to limit access to the abortion drug mifepristone, rather than challenges to more permissive laws adopted in Democratic-led states.

The case is Women's Life Care Center v. Ellison, 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals, No. 25-2905.

For the plaintiffs: Derek Cassidy of Cassidy Law Firm

For the state: Margaret Jacot of the Minnesota Attorney General's Office

For the non-state defendants: Simon de Carvalho of Jenner & Block

New Jersey Resources Corporation () today reported financial and operating results for its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter and year-ended September 30, 2026.

Financial Highlights

Fiscal Year

  • Fiscal 2026 consolidated net income totaled $368.4 million, or $3.65 per share, compared with $335.6 million, or $3.35 per share, in fiscal 2025

  • Fiscal 2026 consolidated net financial earnings (NFE), a non-GAAP financial measure, totaled $361.6 million, or $3.58 per share, compared with $329.6 million, or $3.29 per share, in fiscal 2025

Quarterly

  • Fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter consolidated net income of $17.3 million, or $0.17 per share, compared with net income of $15.1 million, or $0.15 per share, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025

  • Fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter consolidated NFE of $10.7 million, or $0.11 per share, compared with $16.2 million, or $0.16 per share, in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025

  • New Jersey Natural Gas (NJNG): Reduced the average customer bill by 9.0% or approximately $158 annually, ahead of the 2026-2027 winter heating season, while continuing to invest in safe, reliable service
    • Further supported customer affordability through a record $101 million investment in SAVEGREEN energy efficiency programs, reducing customers energy use and bills

    • Through energy assistance outreach, NJNG connected customers with approximately $21 million in bill payment assistance



  • Clean Energy Ventures (CEV): Placed 14 commercial solar projects into service during fiscal 2026, adding 72.4 megawatts (MW)* of capacity and bringing total in-service commercial solar capacity to approximately 552 MW

  • Storage and Transportation (S&T):

NJNG reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net financial loss of $(24.4) million, compared with $(8.0) million during the same period in fiscal 2025. The decrease in NFE for the period was driven primarily by higher depreciation expense as a result of additional utility plant being placed into service and higher interest expense, partially offset by higher utility gross margin.

Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $214.0 million, compared with NFE of $213.5 million in fiscal 2025. The increase is due primarily to the full-year impact of base rates that became effective November 21, 2024, compared with the partial-year impact recognized in fiscal 2025, along with customer growth and SAVEGREEN investments, partially offset by higher depreciation expense from additional plant placed in service.

Customers:

  • At September 30, 2026, NJNG serviced approximately 596,000 customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean, Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties, compared to approximately 589,000 customers as of September 30, 2025.

Regulatory Filings:

  • On June 1, 2026, NJNG submitted its annual Basic Gas Supply Service (BGSS), Conservation Incentive Program (CIP) and energy-efficiency filings to the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (BPU). Taken together, the filings were designed to reduce the average residential customer bill by 9.0%, or approximately $158 annually, ahead of the 2026–2027 winter season. The proposed rate changes were subsequently approved on a provisional basis by the BPU and became effective October 1, 2026.

  • Also, on June 1, 2026, NJNG filed a base rate case with the BPU, seeking a $157.6 million increase to its base rates. The filing is based on an overall rate of return on rate base of 7.60 percent with a return on common equity of 10.10 percent. The proposed increase reflects a 55.50 percent common equity component. On September 21, 2026, the filing was updated to reflect actual results through July 31, 2026, which modified the requested increase to approximately $158.3 million and changed the Company’s overall rate of return on rate base to 7.52 percent.

  • Once all filings are implemented, NJNG anticipates that the overall net result will leave NJNG annualized average customer bills nearly flat. Unless otherwise noted, NJNG cannot predict the outcome or ultimate resolution for open regulatory matters.

  • On September 30, 2026, NJNG filed a letter petition asking the BPU to approve Program Year 7 (PY7), which would continue its SAVEGREEN program through June 30, 2028. The filing has two options: a $127.0 million program based on the BPU's PY7 Framework and a $125.5 million alternative proposed by NJNG. Each option would raise annual recoveries by approximately $17.0 million starting July 1, 2027, if approved.

BGSS Incentive Programs1:

  • BGSS incentive programs contributed $22.8 million to utility gross margin during fiscal 2026, compared with $18.4 million for the same period in fiscal 2025. This increase was primarily driven by increased margins from off-system sales and capacity release due to market volatility as a result of colder than normal weather.

1 BGSS incentive savings represent value created through supply and capacity optimization and shared with customers through the BGSS clause.

For more information on utility gross margin, please see "Non-GAAP Financial Information" below.

Energy-Efficiency Programs:

  • SAVEGREEN® invested $101.0 million in fiscal 2026 in energy-efficiency upgrades for customers' homes and businesses. Investments in SAVEGREEN® are incremental to rate base and earn near-real time returns through an annual recovery mechanism.

  • More than 115,000 customers have taken part in SAVEGREEN® to date, with those utilizing our whole home offerings realizing bill savings of up to 30%.

Clean Energy Ventures (CEV)
CEV reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter NFE of $33.5 million, compared with $23.8 million during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, reflecting higher Renewable Energy Credits and electricity revenue, partially offset by higher depreciation and interest expense associated with capital invested over the past year.

Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $37.6 million, compared with NFE of $61.2 million in fiscal 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a gain from the sale of CEV's residential solar portfolio assets that was recognized in the prior year period.

Solar Investment Update:

  • During fiscal 2026, CEV placed fourteen commercial projects into service, adding 72.4 MW* to installed capacity.

  • As of September 30, 2026, CEV had approximately 552 MW of commercial solar capacity in service across New Jersey, New York, Connecticut, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Indiana, Michigan and Maine.

* All MWs noted in DC

Storage and Transportation (S&T)
S&T reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter NFE of $9.6 million, compared with $4.6 million during the same period in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $33.4 million, compared with NFE of $18.5 million in fiscal 2025.

NFE increased during both periods mainly due to higher operating income at Adelphia Gateway primarily due to the impact of its rate case settled on November 4, 2025 and higher firm storage rates at Leaf River.

Energy Services (ES)
ES reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net financial loss of $(7.9) million, compared with net financial loss of $(4.5) million for the same period in fiscal 2025.

Fiscal 2026 NFE totaled $76.7 million, compared with NFE of $34.9 million for the same period in fiscal 2025. The increase in NFE was primarily due to higher natural gas price volatility that allowed ES to capture additional financial margin.

Home Services and Other Operations
Home Services and Other Operations reported fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter net financial loss of $(1.0) million, compared with net financial loss of $(0.8) million for the same period in fiscal 2025. Fiscal 2026 net financial loss totaled $(0.1) million, compared with net financial loss of $(0.4) million in fiscal 2025.

Capital Expenditures and Cash Flows:

  • Fiscal 2026 capital expenditures, including accruals, were $734.3 million compared with $752.5 million in fiscal 2025.

  • NJR expects to deploy between $5.3 billion and $5.7 billion in capital expenditures from fiscal 2027 through fiscal 2031, with utility spending at NJNG representing over 60% of the investment and strategic growth opportunities at CEV and S&T supporting long-term value creation.

  • During fiscal 2026, cash flows from operations increased to $641.2 million, compared to cash flows from operations of $466.3 million in fiscal 2025, due primarily to an increase in financial margin at ES.

About New Jersey Resources

New Jersey Resources () is a diversified energy infrastructure and energy services company headquartered in Wall, New Jersey.

NJR is composed of five primary businesses:

  • New Jersey Natural Gas, NJR’s principal subsidiary, operates and maintains natural gas transportation and distribution infrastructure to serve customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean, Morris, Middlesex, Sussex and Burlington counties.

  • Clean Energy Ventures invests in, owns and operates solar projects, providing customers with low-carbon solutions.

  • Energy Services manages a diversified portfolio of natural gas transportation and storage assets and provides physical natural gas services and customized energy solutions to its customers across North America.

  • Storage and Transportation serves customers from local distributors and producers to electric generators and wholesale marketers through its ownership of Leaf River and the Adelphia Gateway pipeline, as well as our 50% equity ownership in the Steckman Ridge natural gas storage facility.

  • Home Services provides service contracts as well as heating, central air conditioning, water heaters, standby generators and other indoor and outdoor comfort products to residential homes throughout New Jersey.

NJR and its almost 1,400 employees are committed to helping customers save energy and money by promoting conservation and encouraging efficiency through Conserve to Preserve® and initiatives such as SAVEGREEN®.

Non-GAAP Financial Information:

This earnings release includes the non-GAAP financial measures NFE/net financial loss, NFE per basic share, financial margin and utility gross margin. A reconciliation of these non-GAAP financial measures to the most directly comparable financial measures calculated and reported in accordance with GAAP can be found below. As an indicator of NJR’s operating performance, these measures should not be considered an alternative to, or more meaningful than, net income or operating revenues as determined in accordance with GAAP. This information has been provided pursuant to the requirements of SEC Regulation G.

NFE and financial margin exclude unrealized gains or losses on derivative instruments related to NJR’s unregulated subsidiaries and certain realized gains and losses on derivative instruments related to natural gas that has been placed into storage at ES, net of applicable tax adjustments as described below. Financial margin also differs from gross margin as defined on a GAAP basis as it excludes certain operations and maintenance expense and depreciation and amortization expenses as well as the effects of derivatives as discussed above. Volatility associated with the change in value of these financial instruments and physical commodity reported on the income statement in the current period. In order to manage its business, NJR views its results without the impacts of the unrealized gains and losses, and certain realized gains and losses, caused by changes in value of these financial instruments and physical commodity contracts prior to the completion of the planned transaction because it shows changes in value currently instead of when the planned transaction ultimately is settled. An annual estimated effective tax rate is calculated for NFE purposes and any necessary quarterly tax adjustment is applied to ES.

NJNG’s utility gross margin is defined as operating revenues less natural gas purchases, sales tax and regulatory rider expenses. This measure differs from gross margin as presented on a GAAP basis as it excludes certain operations and maintenance expense and depreciation and amortization. Utility gross margin may also not be comparable to the definition of gross margin used by others in the natural gas distribution business and other industries. Management believes that utility gross margin provides a meaningful basis for evaluating utility operations since natural gas costs, sales tax and regulatory rider expenses are included in operating revenues and passed through to customers and, therefore, have no effect on utility gross margin.

Management uses these non-GAAP financial measures as supplemental measures to other GAAP results to provide a more complete understanding of NJR’s performance. Management believes these non-GAAP financial measures are more reflective of NJR’s business model, provide transparency to investors and enable period-to-period comparability of financial performance. data.title: Brazil Senate approves fiscal package as government seeks to calm markets
data.description:
By Marcela Ayres

Brazil's Senate approved on Wednesday a a fiscal package that the government sees as essential to meet its fiscal targets and investors view as only a first step toward addressing the country's worsening debt outlook.

Backed by recently reelected President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the bill combines spending restraints and revenue-raising measures expected to improve public finances by up to 60 billion reais ($10.29 billion) in 2027.

The package, which now heads to the lower house of Congress, was approved as Finance Minister Dario Durigan sought to reassure markets shaken by mounting fiscal concerns, pledging further action to strengthen public finances.

"We are going to adopt new and additional measures right away," Durigan said on Wednesday, while ruling out changes to Brazil's 3% inflation target or any form of capital controls.

His remarks came amid renewed pressure on Brazil's real , which settled down 1.5% against the US dollar on Wednesday as markets also weighed expectations of higher US interest rates.

The Brazilian currency has weakened about 15% since leftist Lula's surprise election win against right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in late October.

Lula's economic team sees the fiscal package as critical to achieving next year's primary surplus target of 0.5% of gross domestic product, while creating room for spending pledges made during the president's campaign, including expanded welfare benefits and support for students.

MARKETS UNDER PRESSURE

Long-dated bond yields climbed and stocks fell on Wednesday, suggesting investors remain unconvinced that Lula — who has yet to name a finance minister for his next term beginning in January — is prepared to pursue deeper spending reforms.

Many economists see such reforms as necessary to stabilize gross debt, which has risen more than 11 percentage points during Lula's current 2023-2027 term to 82.9% of GDP.

The Senate vote also highlighted political hurdles facing the government before it confronts an even more conservative Congress set to take office in February.

Although the package was seen as modest by most analysts, its approval was delayed after the administration did not secure enough support for a Senate vote on Tuesday.

The measure passed only after the government abandoned plans to retain a larger share of transfers owed to states over the coming years. Analysts, however, said that the concession does not change the bill's core objective.

The bill allows additional budget freezes when needed to meet fiscal goals, activating a cap on annual real spending growth of 2%, below the 2.5% ceiling allowed under the current fiscal framework.

It also cuts tax breaks and creates a mechanism to restrict the use of tax credits, boosting revenue.

DETERIORATING DEBT SCENARIO

Economists have welcomed the proposal as a step in the right direction, but many argue it falls short of addressing Brazil's core fiscal challenge: the relentless expansion of mandatory spending.

Next year, the country's budget is set to leave only 8% of expenditures under discretionary control.

BTG Pactual economist Tiago Berriel, a former central bank director, said in a note the bill improves the 2027 primary balance by about 0.2 percentage points of GDP, but does little to alter Brazil's debt trajectory.

The bank estimates gross public debt would now rise to 118% of GDP by 2034, versus 121% without the measure, arguing that public debt would only stabilize by 2030 if annual expenditure growth were limited to 1%.

($1 = 5.8309 reais)
